question.text: The Total Expense Ratio (TER) of a mutual fund scheme represents:

answer.text: Expenses as a percentage of daily average net assets managed by the fund
The exit load charged when investors redeem their units
The commission paid to distributors for selling the scheme
The total amount of money invested by all unit holders

explanation.text: The Logic: Running expenses of a mutual fund scheme are calculated as a percentage of the daily average net assets (commonly referred to as AUM) managed by the fund. These include investment management fees and operational costs. The expenses are already reflected in (i.e., deducted from) the NAV, so investors do not pay them separately. The Trap: Exit load is a separate charge and is not part of TER. Distributor commission, where payable, is funded out of the TER rather than being a stand-alone charge to the investor. TER is a ratio (percentage), not an absolute amount, and the categories of expenses chargeable plus their upper limits are prescribed by SEBI. Note: TER is disclosed on the AMC's website on a daily basis and is one of the most important comparison metrics across schemes within the same category.
